1. `EventBus` is defined but never exported through `API`, so consumers cannot access it at all; the runtime export surface contains only `version`, `math`, `geom`, `color`, `physics`, `ui`, `webgl`, and `mount`, and `hasEventBus` was false in the load test. 

2. `isNode`, `dpr`, and `now` are also dead private helpers from the public API perspective; the export check showed `hasIsNode`, `hasDpr`, and `hasNow` were all false, so the file carries unused surface-detection utilities that cannot be consumed externally. 

3. `now` uses `isBrowser && performance ? performance.now() : Date.now()`, which can throw a `ReferenceError` in any environment where `isBrowser` is true but `performance` is not bound as an identifier, because the code reads the bare global instead of `globalThis.performance` or `window.performance`.

4. `EventBus.once()` unregisters the wrapper only after the callback returns successfully, so if the callback throws, the supposed one-shot listener remains subscribed and will fire again on later emits.

5. `EventBus.emit()` iterates the live `Set` directly, so listener mutation during dispatch can alter iteration order and produce skipped or unexpectedly added callback executions in the same emit cycle.

6. `gauss(x, sigma)` has no guard for `sigma <= 0`, so `sigma = 0` produces division-by-zero behavior and `x = 0, sigma = 0` yields an undefined `0 / 0` path.

7. `smoothstep(e0, e1, x)` and `smootherstep(e0, e1, x)` divide by `(e1 - e0)` without handling `e0 === e1`, so identical edges produce non-finite math.

8. `roundTo(v, step)` does not validate `step`, and the dynamic check for `roundTo(3, 0)` serialized as `null`, which is what `JSON.stringify` does for a non-finite numeric result, showing the helper breaks on zero step instead of failing safely or returning a sensible fallback. 

9. `sdCapsule()` divides by `dot2(bax, bay, bax, bay)` without guarding the degenerate case where segment start and end are identical, and the dynamic zero-length test also serialized as `null`, again indicating a non-finite result rather than a valid signed distance. 

10. `GkTag._patch()` rewrites `shadowRoot.innerHTML` wholesale whenever the rendered template string changes, which destroys and recreates the entire shadow subtree on each update instead of patching nodes.

11. Because `GkButton` and `GkToggle` animate via `requestAnimationFrame()` and call `_patch()` on changing spring values, they rebuild their whole shadow DOM every animation frame, causing unnecessary allocation, layout churn, and avoidable focus/selection instability.

12. `GkButton` sets `role="button"` and `tabindex="0"` on the host, but pressing Enter or Space only changes animation state; it does not synthesize activation behavior such as `click`, so keyboard users can “press” the control visually without triggering the actual action.

13. `GkButton` does not call `preventDefault()` for Space key activation, so pressing Space on the focused host can scroll the page while the component is trying to behave like a button.

14. `GkButton` handles `pointerup` and `pointerleave` but not `pointercancel`, so interrupted gestures can leave the pressed-state spring transition out of sync with the real pointer lifecycle.

15. `GkButton` exposes a button-like host that contains an actual `<button>` in shadow DOM, creating duplicated interactive semantics instead of one clean control surface.

16. `GkToggle` advertises `role="switch"` and is focusable, but it only toggles on `click`; there is no Enter/Space keyboard support, so it is not operable as a switch for keyboard-only users.

17. `GkToggle` hardcodes the spring destination to `20`, tightly coupling behavior to the current 52px track and 28px knob geometry; any styling change to size immediately breaks travel distance correctness.

18. `GLContextHost` sets `this.isWebGL2 = this.gl instanceof WebGL2RenderingContext;` without first checking whether `WebGL2RenderingContext` exists, so a browser that successfully falls back to WebGL1 but lacks that global can throw at construction time.

19. `createShader()` leaks shader objects on compile failure because it throws without deleting the failed shader, and it also never deletes successfully compiled shaders after program linkage.

20. `createProgram()` leaks resources on link failure because it throws without deleting the program or cleaning up the attached shaders, and even on success it never detaches or deletes the shader objects after linking.

that’s all.

1. `EventBus` is not exported, so it is unreachable from the public API even though it is a complete class inside the module.[1][2][3]

2. `isNode`, `dpr`, and `now` are also private-only helpers and cannot be accessed by consumers, which makes them dead public surface rather than usable utilities.[2][3]

3. `now()` uses the bare identifier `performance` in a way that can fail if that global is not bound, instead of reading it from a safer namespace reference.  

4. `EventBus.once()` only unregisters after the callback returns, so if the callback throws, the listener can remain installed and fire again later.

5. `EventBus.emit()` iterates the live listener `Set` directly, so mutation during dispatch can change which callbacks run in the same emission.

6. `gauss(x, sigma)` has no protection for zero or negative `sigma`, so invalid input can produce non-finite math.

7. `smoothstep(e0, e1, x)` divides by `e1 - e0` without handling equal edges, so `e0 === e1` is undefined behavior.

8. `smootherstep(e0, e1, x)` has the same equal-edge divide-by-zero flaw as `smoothstep`.

9. `roundTo(v, step)` does not validate `step`; the zero-step probe returned a non-finite result that serialized as `null`, showing the function breaks on `step = 0` instead of failing safely.[4][5]

10. `sdCapsule()` divides by the squared segment length with no guard for a zero-length segment, and the zero-length probe also serialized as `null`, confirming a degenerate-case failure.[4]

11. `GkTag._patch()` replaces the entire shadow DOM with `innerHTML` whenever the template string changes, which is a blunt and expensive update strategy.

12. Because `GkButton` re-renders on every spring step, it rebuilds its whole shadow tree every animation frame while animating, causing avoidable DOM churn.

13. `GkButton` uses `role="button"` plus `tabindex="0"` instead of a native button host, but it does not synthesize activation on keyboard press, so keyboard users can focus it without triggering the action.[6][7]

14. `GkButton` does not prevent default on Space handling, so the page can scroll while the control is being “pressed” from the keyboard.[7][6]

15. `GkButton` does not handle `pointercancel`, so interrupted pointer sequences can leave the pressed animation in the wrong state.

16. `GkButton` contains an actual `<button>` inside shadow DOM while the host itself is also made button-like, which duplicates interactive semantics unnecessarily.[8]

17. `GkToggle` only toggles on `click`; it lacks explicit Enter/Space keyboard activation even though it is focusable and declares `role="switch"`.[9][6]

18. `GkToggle` hardcodes the spring target to `20`, so its animation distance is tightly coupled to one exact geometry and breaks if the styling changes.

19. `GLContextHost` computes `this.isWebGL2 = this.gl instanceof WebGL2RenderingContext;` without guarding whether `WebGL2RenderingContext` exists, which can fail in environments that only expose WebGL1.

20. `createShader()` leaks shader objects on compile failure because it throws without deleting the failed shader.[10][11]

21. `createProgram()` leaks both the program object and attached shaders on link failure because it throws before cleanup.[12][13]

22. `createProgram()` also never detaches or deletes shaders after a successful link, so shader resources remain held longer than necessary.[13][12]

23. The module’s UMD wrapper uses a global assignment fallback, but it never exports the private helpers globally, so the top-level wrapper behavior and the internal utility design are mismatched.[1][2]

24. The API surface is very uneven: many general-purpose helpers are defined, but only some are exposed, making the file harder to reuse as a coherent utility library.[14][3]

25. `Rect.contains()` treats the right and bottom edges as inclusive, which can produce overlap/counting ambiguities when rectangles are tiled edge-to-edge.

26. `Rect.intersects()` has the same inclusive-edge behavior, which means rectangles that merely touch edges count as intersecting.

27. `Rect.unionWith()` and `Rect.intersectWith()` mutate `this` in place, which is fine for a mutable geometry type but easy to misuse if callers expect non-destructive behavior.

28. `solveContrastLift()` performs a binary search over luminance, but the search direction logic is tied to a `backdropLum > 0.5` heuristic rather than directly solving for the lighter/darker branch, so it is more fragile than necessary.
